newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian dlr dithers, dogged by rate doubts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian dlr dithers, dogged by rate doubts.

text.p: The Australian dollar languished in the middle of a tight two-week old range Wednesday as uncertainty over domestic interest rates continued to dominate.

What action there was came on the crosses where the local currency tagged along when its U.S. counterpart jumped in relief after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan steered clear of alarming U.S. share and bond markets, traders said.

The AUD, as a perceived member of the dollar bloc and still a nominal high yielder, sneaked up on the yen and most European currencies but was noticeably subdued against the U.S. dollar itself pointing to further risks for the downside.
By 4.45 pm (0545 GMT) the dollar had drooped to US$0.7768/73 on very light volumes from an early US$0.7771/76 and US$0.7773/78 late Tuesday.

Immediate support was put at US$0.7755, with the recent low of US$0.7738 a well defined floor for the currency. Resistance was seen at US$0.7795 while repeated failures at US$0.7820 had made that level the crucial ceiling for most chart watchers.
Analysts reckoned that after two weeks of confinement a break of either could unleash an impulsive move of around 1/2 cent, with US$0.7680 and US$0.7865 the key targets in each direction.
The situation was more fluid on the crosses where widespread expectations of low rates in much of Europe and Japan was forcing a wholesale exodus to higher yielding assets.

This still included the Australian dollar, although three domestic rate cuts last year had seen it lose most-favoured status to the U.S. dollar, and helped it up to 91.83/93 yen and 1.2684/96 marks from 91.53/63 and 1.2603/10 late Tuesday.
In trade weighted terms the currency was steady at 58.6.
Traders said fund flows out of the Swiss franc were particularly heavy as investors everywhere looked to borrow at very low Swiss rates and lend abroad for a fat profit.

That propelled the local dollar to a 4-1/2 year high of 1.1060/73 from 1.0979/90 late Tuesday. The emphatic break of 1.1000 resistance was seen as strongly bullish for the currency and opened the way for a rally to 1.1500 francs and even 1.1900.

The main event of the offshore session had been Greenspan's testimony to a House banking committee in which he offered an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy -- important for the AUD since a strong U.S. bodes well for commodity prices.
Greenspan did warn about wages, but analysts did not sense the sort of urgency that would point to a possible rate hike at the next Fed Committee meeting on February 5 and 6.
Such a tightening would have further narrowed the A$'s yield premium, already pared by 150 basis points of domestic cuts since late July.

Dollar bulls also had a nightmare scenario where the Reserve Bank cut rates by 0.5 point on February 5, only to be followed by a 0.25 point Fed hike later that day. Such an outcome would leave short term rates in both countries at 5.5 percent.

The risk of an RBA move still lingered, although last week's revelation that employment growth had been underestimated since August had made some think the bank would wait for the impact of its last three cuts to show through.

The dollar's recent fall leant support to that view since it represented a de facto easing, analysts said. The drop was most pronounced against the U.S. dollar where it was down 2.3 percent since December, while in trade weighted terms the currency was off a more modest 1.5 percent.
The chances of another easing here should be clearer once December quarter inflation data are known, but these are not due for a week.
Underlying inflation is expected to slow to around 2.2 percent in annual terms from 2.4 percent in Q3 and a peak of 3.3 percent a year ago. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
